question: A bulk cement delivery shows unexpected chloride in the receiving silo after a tanker previously carried a different powder. How should an independent research agent investigate possible residual-cargo contamination without blaming the carrier or recommending silo release prematurely?
category: Bulk tanker prior-cargo contamination and chloride provenance
scenario: Unexpected chloride result in cement after pneumatic tanker discharge with disputed cleaning history
evidence_required: Tanker compartment identity, previous cargo manifests, washout/cleaning and dry-out certificates, loading seals and chain-of-custody records
Pre-loading cement retained samples, tanker loading and discharge samples, silo pre-receipt samples, sampling point and timestamp records
Accredited laboratory chloride method, replicate uncertainty, silo mass balance, existing stock quantity, possible alternative chloride inputs and contractual acceptance specification
answer_and_decision_guide: Quarantine the affected lot according to site quality procedures, reconcile each sample to a physical mass and time boundary, then compare retained pre-loading material, tanker residues and silo background. Check whether the laboratory method, sample handling or silo mixing could explain the result before attributing contamination to the previous cargo. Use independent testing and applicable specification/contract to decide disposition; no generic chloride acceptance threshold or liability determination is justified.
source_provenance: Seller-maintained directory is navigation, not independent evidence of tanker cleaning or cement chloride acceptance. Verify applicable cement standard, laboratory method and carrier documents directly.
free_first_decision: First use plant QA records, freely accessible applicable standard summaries, original manifests and independent laboratory reports; a paid library is unnecessary if these resolve the question.

conditional_paid_check.authorization: Before any paid reference, confirm the exact filename, edition, permissions, current seller price and buyer's explicit purchase authorization. Never transact automatically.

model_limitations: No physical samples, manifest, certified chloride results or contract provided. Cannot conclude contamination source, safety, conformity or carrier responsibility.
